There are several individuals named Evan Huang who are software engineers, each with distinct specializations and contributions.

One prominent Evan Huang is a Software Engineer at Capital One, based in McLean, VA. His work encompasses building cave-survey devices, backend services, and developer tools, with projects spanning embedded firmware, web applications, and local AI. At Capital One, he developed "Recadero," a Go CLI adopted by several production services to streamline event contract generation, and built a billing-cycle management action for credit card processing. He also designed an event-driven card transaction processing system and contributed to preapproval and eligibility flows for a small-business credit card platform, generating significant annualized value. His past experience includes software engineering internships at Capital One, where he worked on a Scala/ZIO verification layer for a transaction ledger and a Spark/Scala pipeline for identifying untracked DynamoDB datasets. He is also the founder of HashTop, a cryptocurrency mining platform. His technical skills include Go, Python, Kafka, Restate, AWS, and React.

Another Evan Huang, described as a "Software Engineer & Solo Dev," is pursuing an MS in Computer Science at New York University, having also completed his BA in Computer Science & Economics there. His portfolio showcases projects in agent simulations, real-time tooling, and "living systems". Notably, he developed "World Engine," an LLM-driven world for autonomous agents, and "Agilee," a real-time collaboration tool for agile meetings. His technical proficiencies include AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, Git, Django, Flask, SQL, Python, and MongoDB.

Additionally, there is an Evan Huang who is a frontend developer active on GitHub under the handle "EvanTechDev". He is passionate about open source and is currently developing "One-Calendar," an AI agent-powered calendar.

Another individual named Evan Huang gained recognition as a RISE Global Winner and VEX Robotics Challenge World Winner for inventing "DrinkBot," a robot designed to assist the elderly and disabled by grabbing and delivering cups. He has continued to develop and improve DrinkBot, motivated by a personal mission to enhance the quality of life for the elderly and disabled.

Several individuals and groups are actively building DIY and open-source hardware for underwater cave mapping:

*   **Tim Hansen and Andreas Birk** have co-authored an open-source software framework for real-time underwater mapping. This system utilizes low-cost marine robotics components, such as the BlueRobotics BlueROV2 with its Ping360 Mechanical Scanning Sonar and an A50 Doppler Velocity Log, running on a Raspberry Pi 4.
*   An individual behind the website **"Caving – Diving – Making"** is developing a DIY underwater survey device. This device is inspired by commercial tools like the Mnemo and is designed to log depth, bearing, temperature, pitch, and roll, aiming to automate and enhance the accuracy of underwater cave surveying.
*   **9nl** has created a DIY sensor system for 3D cave mapping. This system uses a Raspberry Pi 5 running ROS2, an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), and a spinning 2D lidar sensor to perform Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) in underground environments.
*   **Nicho Hadinata** is the developer of "SeaSphere," an open-source, lightweight, spherical, autonomous device for sea-mapping. SeaSphere integrates modular sensors like an IMU, sonar, and GPS, and Hadinata is seeking collaborators for its further development.
*   **Neumi** is in the process of developing a DIY open-source SONAR/Echo Sounder/Fishfinder/Depth Sounder, utilizing an Arduino Uno for data acquisition.
*   **Phil Underwood** is involved in building an open-source tool for cave surveying, which has been featured on the element14 Community.
*   **The Cave Pearl Project** focuses on creating open-source underwater data loggers. These versatile loggers, initially designed for flow sensors, have evolved into a platform for various environmental monitoring applications, emphasizing modularity and accessibility for tinkerers.
*   The **3D-CAVE Project** at INESC-ID is researching and developing solutions for 3D reconstruction and real-time mapping in flooded caves. This project explores advanced algorithmic improvements and the use of low-power VI-SLAM hardware accelerators on embedded Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) devices, often integrated with Diver Propulsion Vehicles (DPVs).
*   **OpenCHIRP** represents another open-source initiative, focusing on a low-cost and lightweight sub-bottom profiler suitable for shallow water environments and autonomous vehicles, though specific individual builders are not named in the provided information.

results.response_text:
The Camazotz cave mapping project primarily refers to the development and ongoing field testing of the "Cave Mapper System" by Camazotz Diving. This is an advanced, integrated underwater cave mapping solution designed to create detailed 3D maps in real time as divers explore.

Key aspects of the Camazotz Cave Mapper System include:
*   **Real-Time 3D Mapping** The system combines multiple sensor inputs to build a real-time model of the cave passage during a dive.
*   **Sensor Integration** It utilizes a high-precision pressure transducer for accurate depth profiling, a magnetic encoder coupled to a wheel for tracking line deployment and measuring distance, and a 9-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) for heading and attitude.
*   **Data Processing** A dual-core processor continuously combines sensor data to plot the diver's position, resulting in a real-time "stick map" of the path through the cave.
*   **Post-Dive Analysis** After a dive, the collected data can be processed to generate 2D passage profiles (plan and cross-section views), 3D point cloud visualizations, and can be exported to standard cave survey formats like Compass and Walls.
*   **Accessibility** Camazotz Diving also offers free, browser-based cave mapping software for visualizing 3D cave surveys, supporting offline use and requiring no installation or accounts.
*   **Customization** The Cave Mapper is custom-built to specifications, allowing for personalization with initials or team markings.

Beyond the specific Cave Mapper System, "Camazotz" is also associated with a broader initiative to create robust and affordable devices for 3D cave mapping, aiming to move beyond traditional 2D sketches to provide more insightful scientific data. This wider project seeks to develop a cheap, robust, and open-source 3D scanning device suitable for harsh cave environments, which can be used by scientists for various studies, including computer simulations and 3D printing of cave structures.

results.response_text:
The Camazotz Cave Mapper System is a project by Camazotz Diving (a custom cave diving gear company) focused on building a fully integrated, automated underwater cave mapping solution .
The project aims to simplify cave surveying by turning standard exploration dives into highly detailed, accurate models.
Key Features of the System
Automated Data Gathering: Instead of using traditional manual underwater survey techniques (which are incredibly difficult in tight, flooded environments), the hardware maps the cave during an active dive.
Post-Dive 3D Processing: After a dive, the user connects the mapper device to a computer to automatically generate 2D passage profiles (plan and cross-section views) as well as 3D point cloud visualizations.
Browser-Based Visualization: The project features an online, open-source platform at map.camazotzdiving.com where divers can securely upload their survey data and render 3D cave paths directly in the browser via WebAssembly without installing software.
Standard Integration: The mapping data can be easily exported into industry-standard land and cave survey programs like Compass and Walls .

Within the context of the story's lore:
Camazotz is a dark planet fully conquered and controlled by the malevolent, disembodied telepathic brain known as IT.

L'Engle named both planets after ancient Mayan deities: Camazotz is named after the Mayan bat god of night and death, while Ixchel is named after the Mayan jaguar goddess of medicine and childbirth.
